state.question: Which video shows an organism using a flat body structure to adapt to its environment?
state.summary: The best-supported option is C. v3 has positive local evidence of a flattened aquatic invertebrate gripping substrate in fast-moving water, which directly matches an organism using a flat body structure to adapt to its environment. v2 shows a pika lying flat but not a flat body adaptation. v1 lacks positive flat-body evidence and remains only partially observed. v4 shows pandas and birds without relevant flat-body adaptation evidence.
inference_protocol: Video IDs identify the normalized input clips/views and must never be inferred from event or slot IDs.
A reasoning cycle is PLAN -> local FOCUS observation -> memory revision -> fresh state projection; completing one cycle does not imply sufficient evidence.
FOCUS evidence is valid only for its cited video and time span; it cannot prove whole-video or cross-video absence.
Count physical entities or transitions, not frames, mentions, or duplicate observations of the same event.
The final answer must be exactly one option label from the supplied choices, never a video ID, option text, refusal, or unknown.
If evidence remains incomplete when no executable visual budget remains, choose the best-supported option label and retain the uncertainty in the summary.

attempts: Local v2 evidence shows a pika lying flat but also describes it as a small, round-bodied rodent; the observed posture does not establish a flat body structure adapted to the environment.

v3 contains direct local evidence of a small flattened aquatic invertebrate in turbulent fast-moving water, with legs gripping the substrate, supporting visible use of a flat body structure as an environmental adaptation.
Sampled v1 aquatic organisms show spiny or segmented forms, but unobserved intervals prevent a global conclusion about flat-body adaptation elsewhere in v1.
